implementation.principals: Keep authenticated canonical profile/connection bound to the native run and call. For an existing openclaw-device grant only, compare its exact ID to separately Host-attested deviceId and use that same device principal in the permission request snapshot. No profile alias or requester grant is created.
implementation.attestation: Only internal.operatorDeviceTokenIdentity from public Gateway scope, requiring authenticatedControlUi+authenticatedOperator and initial hasCurrentClientAuthority true; accept64lowercasehex deviceId. Never read connect.device as evidence or token-generation key.
implementation.grantSelection: The exact existing grant determines device vs explicit profile principal. A profile string equal to a device-form requester is insufficient without attestation. Existing explicit profile grants retain their semantics.
implementation.lifetime: Capture scalar identity once; each protected hook/read rechecks same profile, connection and device fact. Conflict poisons that native run. Initial live admission per new request; native admitted continuation can survive completed RPC/transport retirement, with cancellation and native/v2 guards unchanged.
implementation.hostFieldsAndPermissions: No Host SenderId/context/profile mutation, no grant edit or alias, no new trusted identity/audience/model/learning permission.

chain: Gateway prepares operator device source from existing paired record using authenticated role/operator public key/token/scopes.
resolveAuthenticatedDeviceTokenIdentity requires matching public key and exact role token, then validates current approved role/scopes and returns a frozen identity.
Only authenticatedOperator connection preparation places that result into internal.operatorDeviceTokenIdentity; public Gateway scope exposes it to the plugin.
Core consumes onlydeviceId; optional/null/tokenless sources cannot satisfy device grants.
